title: Scryer — C4 Architecture Diagram MCP for Agent Context Grounding
description: Desktop app that ships a bundled MCP server. The agent uses MCP tools to read and modify a C4 architecture diagram, which renders in real-time in a visual drag-and-drop editor. Key value: a shared, persistent architecture model that both developer and agent read from and write to — specifically to prevent context drift where an agent loses architectural understanding across sessions. Auto-detects Claude Code and Codex installations and writes project-scoped MCP config.
redundancy_notes: No architecture diagram or visual model MCP in registry. Closest entries are code-review-graph (knowledge graph for token reduction, NEEDS_RESEARCH), contextplus (blast radius analysis, rejected due to Ollama dependency), and mgrep (semantic file search). None provide a human-readable visual architecture model persisting across sessions that is both human- and agent-editable.

evaluation.reasoning: Score sits solidly in the 50-69 NEEDS_RESEARCH band. The capability gap is real — context drift across sessions is a genuine pain point with no current mitigation — and the problem being solved is novel (score: 80). However, the desktop app delivery model introduces integration friction not present in a pure npm MCP (score: 60), and the community validation is weak at <100 GitHub stars with no official backing (score: 45). Key unknowns blocking APPROVED decision: (1) exact GitHub star count to confirm community validation score, (2) whether the MCP server can be run without the desktop app GUI (headless/server mode), (3) license terms. Token efficiency is marginal — architecture context reduces drift but doesn't directly reduce tokens in normal operation (score: 55). Maintenance concern: desktop app updates are user-managed, not auto-updated like npm packages (score: 65).
evaluation.action: NEEDS_RESEARCH: (1) Check GitHub star count for aklos/scryer. (2) Investigate whether MCP server component can run headless without GUI. (3) Review license. If star count crosses 100 and headless mode is confirmed, re-evaluate — could reach 70+ with those unknowns resolved.
